author: Rachel Kim - Technology Editor
title: Magene GPS Bike Computer: Garmin Features at a Fraction of the Cost
text:
Magene has released a GPS cycling computer priced at 2,259 CZK, offering navigation and mapping features typically found in higher-end devices from competitors like Garmin, according to reporting by MobilMania.cz.
What features does the Magene cycling computer provide? The device includes integrated GPS and map support for route navigation. According to MobilMania.cz, the computer is positioned as a budget-friendly alternative that replicates the core functionality of premium cycling computers. The hardware allows riders to track their position and follow mapped paths without the cost associated with industry-standard high-end models.
How does Magene’s pricing compare to Garmin? Magene is marketing the device at a “fraction of the price” of Garmin units. While the specific Garmin model used for comparison isn’t named, the 2,259 CZK price point targets the entry-level and mid-range market. MobilMania.cz notes that the primary value proposition is the inclusion of mapping and GPS capabilities at a price significantly lower than the typical retail cost of a Garmin Edge series device.
Why does the price point matter for cyclists? The availability of mapping functions at this price level lowers the barrier for cyclists who require navigation but cannot justify the expense of professional-grade hardware. By offering these specific tools—GPS and maps—for 2,259 CZK, Magene is competing directly with the “budget” segments of the cycling electronics market.
Availability and further technical specifications remain tied to regional distributors and Magene’s official product listings.
